newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish/German yield gap seen wider by Sept - poll.
newsitem.headline: Finnish/German yield gap seen wider by Sept - poll.

text.p: The gap between the yields on Finnish 7.25-pct 2006 government benchmark bonds and on German 6.00-pct Bunds maturing in 2007 is expected to widen to 35 basis points by September, according to a Reuters poll.
The median of forecasts by 23 dealers, economists and analysts at banks and corporate treasury departments was 35 basis points.
Three respondents saw the yield gap widening to 45 bps while one expected it to narrow to 20 bps by September.
Looking one year ahead, the Finnish/German yield gap was seen narrowing to around 25 bps.
One operator expected the gap to shrink to nil, while three respondents forecast a widening spread up to 40 bps.
The poll was conducted by telephone on May 22 and 23 -- before the first round of the French general election on Sunday -- and the forecasts were collected on an anonymous basis.
The long-end yield gap over Germany widened to 33 bps on Monday on uncertainty whether EMU will start on time if the French opposition socialists win the second round next Sunday.

Forecasts by Aktia Bank, Bank of America (London), Banque Indosuez (Stockholm), CD Derivatives Ltd., Davy Protos, Den Danske Bank (Copenhagen), Enso, Handelsbaken Markets Finland, Huhtamaki Finance, I.D.E.A. (London), Interbank, IVO, Kemira, Kesko, Merita Bank, Neste, Nokia, OKOBANK, Postipankki, SE-Banken Helsinki, SOK, Unibank (Copenhagen) and UPM-Kymmene.
